name: Hammam ibn Yahya
nameAr: همام بن يحيى بن دينار العوذي المحلمي مولاهم، أبو عبد الله، البصري

orthography.spelled: al-Awdhi: fathah on the ayn, sukun on the waw, kasrah on the dhal

diedNote: 164 or 165 AH (Taqrib); the Shamela record also gives 163

deathVariants.authority: as given on the Shamela record

teachers.name: Qatadah ibn Di'amah
teachers.source: Ibn Hajar, Hady al-Sari, ch. 9, letter ha' (Hammam among the companions of Qatadah)

verdicts.en: Hammam is firm in all the shaykhs.

verdicts.ar: همام عندي في الصدق مثل ابن أبي عروبة
verdicts.en: To me Hammam is the equal of Ibn Abi Arubah in truthfulness.

verdicts.ar: أحد الأثبات … وهذا يقتضي أن حديث همام بآخرة أصح ممن سمع منه قديما، وقد نص على ذلك أحمد بن حنبل، وقد اعتمده الأئمة الستة
verdicts.en: One of the firm narrators. Reviewing Yahya al-Qattan's reservations and Affan's report that Hammam later checked his books and corrected himself, he concludes that Hammam's hadith from his later period is sounder than what was heard from him early, as Ahmad stated, and that the six imams relied on him.

flags.label: Yahya al-Qattan's reservation
flags.detail: Al-Qattan paid little regard to Hammam and objected to much of his hadith; when Mu'adh ibn Hisham's books were checked they agreed with Hammam on many of the points Yahya had denied, and Yahya desisted. Hammam himself said that after returning to his books he found “we used to err a great deal” (Hady al-Sari, ch. 9). Ibn Sa'd: reliable, he sometimes erred in hadith.

flags.label: Sole transmitter from Thabit, with support
flags.detail: Al-Tirmidhi and al-Bazzar said the cave hadith is known only through Hammam from Thabit. Ibn Hajar adds that Ibn Shahin's al-Afrad has it from Ja'far ibn Sulayman from Thabit as a corroboration, with witnesses from Habashi ibn Janadah (Ibn Asakir) and Ibn Abbas (al-Hakim, al-Iklil) (Fath al-Bari on 3653).

bio: A Basran client of the seventh generation and one of the chief transmitters of Qatadah and Yahya ibn Abi Kathir, used by all six compilers. Ahmad called him firm in every shaykh, and the hesitation of Yahya al-Qattan was answered in Yahya's own lifetime. In the cave hadith he is the pivot: three Basran students of his carry it to al-Bukhari.
